header.title: Rate, political and AI-power forces have pressured utilities as an AI enabler

s01_bottom_line.text: The article says utilities, key enablers of the AI data center build-out, have underperformed (around -10% since May) due to state data center moratoriums (New York, Texas) and rising Treasury yields competing with their dividends. ⟨cited figures: approximate, read from a chart; data as of 2026-09-30⟩
The article presents utilities as a microcosm encapsulating AI's economic promise, the political consequences of the investment boom and the reality of higher rates.

The article documents the drivers of utilities' underperformance but does not quantify the earnings impact of moratoriums or state whether the sector is now oversold, so it is a descriptive pressure case rather than an entry-point call.

items.text: S&P 500 Utilities peaked above 10% price return in July then fell to around -10% by end September (since May). ⟨cited figures: approximate, read from a chart; data as of 2026-09-30⟩
S&P 500 Utilities price and P/E peaked before the New York data center moratorium and fell sharply after the Texas data center restrictions in early August.
State governments have put moratoriums on data center build-out, weighing on the utilities sector.
Utilities are key enablers of the AI data center build-out because few power sources can handle its scale.
Rising Treasury yields compete with utilities' dividends, weighing on the sector.
